items.title: Exact Fisher energy of the restricted-Gaussian fiber score

source.anchor: Lemma 2 proof, the Fisher-information display immediately before equation (11); used by SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1 Lemma 4.17
source.attribution: Yin Tat Lee, Ruoqi Shen and Kevin Tian; used by Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. ASTIS isolates the explicit-representative integration step; no author endorsement implied.

items.statement: Under the left restricted-Gaussian probability fiber, the explicit normalized quadratic log-ratio representative has constant score eta^{-1}(y-y'), so its relative Fisher energy is exactly eta^{-2} times the squared center displacement. This is one input to the cited LSI/Talagrand route, not the resulting Wasserstein contraction.
assumptions: The common normalization base and the probability law used for the expectation are separate measures; the source expectation law is the left tilt of the common base.
The paper has eta>0; the algebraic integration theorem needs only eta nonzero.
The smooth displayed representative is used. Almost-everywhere agreement with a canonical llr does not transfer classical differentiability.

obligations.label: Evaluate the relative Fisher functional of the explicit quadratic log-ratio representative

bindings.boundary: Exact probability integral of the explicit constant score only. Canonical-score domains, LSI, T2, W2 and kernel contraction remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: The expectation is under the normalized left restricted-Gaussian fiber with eta>0.
assumption_deltas.lean: Any common normalization measure nu, any separate probability integration law mu on finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and eta!=0.
assumption_deltas.reason: After the exact score has been proved, only probability mass one and nonzero eta enter the integration step. Separating nu from mu permits the actual source specialization; constructing mu as the normalized left fiber remains a separate adapter.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper writes Fisher information of the displayed density ratio.
assumption_deltas.lean: RelativeFisher.information is evaluated on that explicit smooth representative, not on an arbitrary canonical measurable llr.
assumption_deltas.reason: Almost-everywhere equality of function values does not determine a classical gradient after null-set changes.

assumption_deltas.source: The Fisher value is inserted into LSI and Talagrand inequalities to obtain a W2 estimate.
assumption_deltas.lean: Only the exact Fisher value is concluded.
assumption_deltas.reason: The strong-convex Gibbs LSI/T2 backend and its actual fiber specialization are independent red obligations.
